hero.title: Talk to Claude about your novel
hero.intro: Add NVS to Claude once, and you can ask Claude anything about your story — what threads are still open, where the plot holes are, what happens in a scene. It reads the same analysis you see in the rails.

getFile.title: Get the plugin file
getFile.body: One file, made for this computer. Save it somewhere you can find it — your Desktop is fine.
getFile.restart: Restart NVS to pick up this feature.
getFile.notBuilt: Not ready in this dev build — run `npm run mcp:build` once. (Shipped copies include it.)

addToClaude.title: Add it to Claude
addToClaude.shotUpload: Claude → Settings → Plugins → Add → Upload plugin
addToClaude.shotPickZip: Pick the file you just saved, then Upload
addToClaude.body: In **Claude Desktop**, open **Settings → Plugins**, click **Add → Upload plugin**, and choose the file. That's it — no accounts, no keys.

ask.title: Type /nvs and ask
ask.shotInstalled: Installed — Claude now has an /nvs skill
ask.intro: In any Claude chat, start your message with `/nvs` and ask in plain words:
examples: /nvs read scene 3 and tell me what it sets up
/nvs what plot holes did you find?
/nvs take a screenshot of my timeline — does it look tangled?
ask.liveNote: **While NVS is open**, Claude follows whatever project you have on screen and can screenshot your rails. Close the app and it still answers — from the project you had open when you made the file.
ask.privacy: Claude works from the analysis in your project folder — your writing never leaves this computer.

advanced.summary: Advanced — Claude Code, and letting Claude see your screen

connect.title: Connect Claude Code to the open app
connect.body: The plugin above already does this for you — it detects the running app and hands off to it. This is the direct connection for **Claude Code** users who'd rather not install the plugin:
connect.tokenWarn: Copy it — don't screenshot or share it. That token lets any local process drive your open project.
connect.needProject: Open a project first — then this command appears.

headless.title: Claude Code, without the app running
headless.body: Same engine, no window — it can also build the analysis for a folder of markdown from scratch. The `--live` path is what lets it hand off to the app whenever that's running.

byHand.title: Claude Desktop by hand
byHand.body: The plugin above does this for you. If you'd rather edit config yourself: **Settings → Developer → Edit Config** (the **Developer** tab — not **Connectors**, which is for cloud servers and can't reach your machine).

advanced.toolsLine: {{n}} engine tools · local connection, not a cloud service.
